rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Only one pair is unresolved, and the last peak is already within 10 minutes. Raise temperature while keeping the gradient fixed to test whether selectivity separates that pair without sacrificing the time score.
Injection 2 reached the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one step to test whether full resolution can be preserved with an earlier last peak.

Restore the successful gradient slope from injection 2 while raising the starting organic fraction to shorten retention. This tests a faster, narrower window without the slope increase that compromised resolution in injection 3.

Keep injection 2 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a faster, hotter gradient. The combined selectivity shift may reverse and separate the current critical pair, though the full peak pattern must be checked for new overlaps.

At 60 C the critical pair appears to have crossed elution order; a steeper gradient may now increase its separation. Shorten by one step to test this faster branch while retaining injection 2 as the maximum-score fallback.

The faster 60 C gradients introduce multiple unresolved pairs, so test the opposite temperature extreme for a different selectivity pattern. Keep the broad solvent window to ensure elution and retain injection 2 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Test a moderate-temperature alternative to the successful 55 C method: cooling below 40 C may separate the critical pair on the opposite side of its selectivity crossover. A 10-minute gradient tests whether that branch can deliver full resolution faster than injection 2.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction separates the crossed critical pair seen at 60 C, using a slightly shallower slope than injection 5. Check both early-peak retention and the neighboring central pair; injection 2 remains the maximum-score fallback.
